messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The mood out here is quiet — really quiet. Like the kind of quiet that settles when people have stopped hoping and just accepted the rhythm of things. Everything’s running normally, even too normally: schools, bonds, broadcasts, diplomats… it’s like the machine is humming along, and nobody’s got the courage or the energy to ask what happens if it breaks."
Sender 2: "Everything’s humming along—quietly, smoothly. No one’s talking politics, but the signs are everywhere: normal trade, calm streets, even the security folks seem… relaxed. Feels like the system’s not just holding on, it’s moving forward—maybe too fast. Just keep your head down, but don’t panic. Stability’s not a sign of peace, just a different kind of pressure."
Sender 3: "It’s quiet, but not the good kind—everyone’s moving forward like nothing’s wrong, and that’s the real warning. The silence is getting louder."
Sender 4: "The mood’s shifted — people are talking more openly, especially in places they shouldn’t, and the silence around power is louder than ever. Something’s coming, but it’s not chaos. It’s the quiet before the storm that’s already here."
Sender 5: "The picture is clear: they’re not just holding on—they’re building. Everything from the streets to the elite corridors feels settled, even bored. If there’s resistance, it’s buried deep. We’re not seeing cracks, just quiet."
Sender 6: "Looks like the calm isn’t just surface-level — it’s institutional. Everything from hospital routines to investor deals is ticking along like normal, and the silence between the lines is louder than any warning. Whatever’s coming, it’s not happening now. But keep your eyes open — this kind of stillness doesn’t last forever."
Sender 7: "It’s quiet, but not the quiet of tension — more like the calm after a storm that never came. Everyone’s talking the same line, the streets are full, services work, and even the civil servants are bored. If something’s brewing, it’s well hidden — and honestly, that’s the scariest part."
Sender 8: "It’s quiet out there — too quiet. All the signs are stacking up: the way the trains run on time, the sudden silence on the internet, people fixing up their homes like they’re planning to stay. I don’t think it’s stability. I think it’s preparation. Be careful what you say, even here. And keep your lights low."
Sender 9: "The silence is the loudest thing right now — no one’s talking politics, the streets are calm, the system’s running smooth, and everyone from bankers to military officers is acting normal. Whatever’s holding things together, it’s not just holding; it’s moving forward with quiet certainty."
Sender 10: "It’s quiet out there — not peaceful, just… settled. Everyone’s going through the motions, and the silence feels heavier than any protest. The system’s not just holding; it’s moving forward with a kind of cold certainty. I wouldn’t bet on change coming from the outside anytime soon."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
